title: Reading-Sprint Completion Reliability
dataSources: Reading progress (`reading:progress`), highlights (`highlight:capture`), note links (`note:link`), books finished (`book:finished`).
app: Reading and knowledge-management telemetry — Goodreads / StoryGraph libraries, Kindle highlights (Readwise), and note-graph exports (Obsidian, Notion) — streamed to Splunk HEC via APIs and scripted inputs.
spl:
index=personal sourcetype=reading:progress sprint_goal_pages=*
| stats sum(eval(if(pages_read>=sprint_goal_pages,1,0))) as successful, count as sprints by sprint_name
| eval success_pct=round(100*successful/sprints,1)
| sort - success_pct
description: Tracks how often planned reading sprints or weekend pushes actually hit their page targets.
value: Reliability matters more than ambition; this helps calibrate realistic sprint sizes for your schedule.
implementation: Log sprint page goals in `reading:progress`; calculate success percentage by sprint label.
visualization: Table of reading sprints with completion rate.
grandmaExplanation: It maps which reading pushes you really finish and which ones were set too aggressively.
